hypotheses.title: More orders-api pods exhaust the database connections
hypotheses.summary: The latest release lets orders-api scale further (HorizontalPodAutoscaler orders-api maxReplicas 6 → 20). Every pod keeps its own connection pool, so the total wanted exceeds what orders-postgresql allows; new connections are refused and requests fail or time out. The same pattern shows in prod-us-west.

evidence.text: orders-api cannot get database connections 7 times (first at 22:36:52 UTC): "HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms (total=13, active=13, idle=0, wai…".
The database orders-postgresql (prod-us-east) is refusing new connections 10 times: "…UTC [29166] FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for roles with the SUPERUSER attribute".
Helm raised the connection demand: HorizontalPodAutoscaler orders-api maxReplicas 6 → 20. Each pod opens its own pool, so more pods means more connections.
The HorizontalPodAutoscaler for orders-api is at its maximum, so the pod count (and the connection count) is as high as it can go.
Other clients of the same database fail the same way (orders-worker).

Same pattern in prod-us-west: orders-api cannot get database connections 3 times (first at 22:40:58 UTC): "HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms (total=9, active=9, idle=0, waiti…".

nextChecks.why: Who holds the connections, and how many are idle.

nextChecks.cmd: kubectl --context prod-us-east -n data exec orders-postgresql-0 -- psql -U postgres -c "SHOW max_connections;"
nextChecks.why: The server limit the pools add up against.
Current and maximum replicas per autoscaler.

nextChecks.cmd: kubectl --context prod-us-east -n orders get deployment/orders-api -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}'
nextChecks.why: Replicas right now (multiply by the pool size per pod).
Prometheus query (postgres_exporter): connections by database and state.
Prometheus query: the configured connection limit.
Prometheus query (Micrometer): threads waiting for a pooled connection per pod.

hypotheses.title: Helm release orders r24 broke orders-api
hypotheses.summary: Helm release orders r23 → r24 changed 8 fields (1 high-risk change) shortly before orders-api started failing.

evidence.text: orders-api first failed 5 min 12 s after the deploy: "orders-api: POST /v1/orders failed — CannotCreateTransactionException: Could not open JPA…".
Helm release orders r23 → r24 rolled out at 22:31:40 UTC, chart orders-3.2.0 → orders-3.3.0.
High-risk change in this release: HorizontalPodAutoscaler orders-api maxReplicas 6 → 20.
Kubernetes rolled out a new ReplicaSet (orders-api-6d8f7b9c54) for orders-api.
Also changed: ConfigMap orders-api-env ORDERS_SPLIT_SHIPMENTS_ENABLED: false → true.

hypotheses.title: orders-api cannot get enough capacity
hypotheses.summary: New orders-api pods cannot be placed (not enough node capacity, a quota or an unbound volume), so the workload cannot scale to meet load.

evidence.text: 1 pod of orders-api cannot be scheduled: "FailedScheduling: 0/24 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient cpu, 18 node(s) didn't match P…".
The autoscaler for orders-api is at its maximum.
Replica settings changed: HorizontalPodAutoscaler orders-api maxReplicas 6 → 20.

against.text: The release raised the replica ceiling (HorizontalPodAutoscaler orders-api maxReplicas 6 → 20); pods waiting for room are a side effect of scaling out further, not a cause of the errors.

hypotheses.title: orders-postgresql is the failing dependency
hypotheses.summary: Callers fail when they call orders-postgresql, and nothing orders-postgresql calls is failing, so the failure starts there.

orders-postgresql reports its own errors 10 times: "2026-10-05 22:36:52.431 UTC [29166] FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for ro…".

rollbacks.title: Roll back Helm release orders to r23 in prod-us-east and prod-us-west
commands: kubectl --context prod-us-east -n orders rollout status deployment/orders-api --timeout=5m
kubectl --context prod-us-west -n orders rollout status deployment/orders-api --timeout=5m
caveats: Helm records the rollback as a new revision (r25) with the contents of r23; r24 stays in the history.

It reverts all of r24's template changes, not only the suspect one: HorizontalPodAutoscaler orders-api maxReplicas 6 → 20; ConfigMap orders-api-env ORDERS_SPLIT_SHIPMENTS_ENABLED: false → true; orders-api image tag 3.2.0 → 3.3.0.
prod-us-east and prod-us-west use one database (orders-postgresql in prod-us-east), and every cluster's connections count against its limit, so rolling back only one cluster is not enough.
If Argo CD or Flux manages this release, pause auto-sync first (argocd app set <app> --sync-policy none, or flux suspend helmrelease orders -n orders), or it will re-apply r24 within minutes.
prerequisites: Access to kube-context prod-us-east and prod-us-west with rights to change namespace orders.
Check that r23 ran without problems before r24: helm history orders -n orders --kube-context prod-us-east --max 5
Confirm prod-us-west runs orders r24 (Helm pane line 8 says so) before its steps: helm history orders -n orders --kube-context prod-us-west --max 5

rollbacks.title: Lower orders-api maxReplicas back to 6
commands: kubectl --context prod-us-east -n orders patch hpa orders-api --type merge -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":6}}'
kubectl --context prod-us-west -n orders patch hpa orders-api --type merge -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":6}}'
caveats: The next helm upgrade sets maxReplicas back to 20 unless the chart values change too.
Pods above the new limit are stopped; requests in flight on them can fail, and peak traffic may need more than 6 pods.
Database connections fall only as pods stop; watch the connection count (pg_stat_activity) drop below the limit.
The command for prod-us-west assumes it runs the same chart values (maxReplicas 6 before the change).
If Argo CD or Flux manages this release, pause auto-sync first (argocd app set <app> --sync-policy none, or flux suspend helmrelease orders -n orders), or it will revert this patch within minutes.
prerequisites: Confirm maxReplicas 6 × the pool size per pod × 2 clusters sharing the database, plus the orders-worker pools, stays under the database limit (SHOW max_connections).
